Now, when I saw those three names and I saw the mention of Bugojno, I wondered whether there were possibly not only two players on the ground, without referring to tu quoque or whatever else, but three players, the Serbs, the Croats, and the Muslims, because everything is connected, and that's why I asked you that question, and I said, If I consider this conflict to be a conflict between two players, am I right in thinking that, or should I consider the context involving three stakeholders or three players? I think it was a clear question. So maybe you knew that or did not know that. Maybe you only dealt with the BH Army and not with the Serbs, and maybe that explains or that can explain a number of things. However, as an analyst working in the VOS, did you have a knowledge about the whole context or did you have a knowledge about only what was happening within the BH Army? That's the gist of my question. So what's your field of competence, only the BH Army or the BH Army and also the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we had knowledge of both what was happening in the BH Army and in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So you had some knowledge about what was happening both within the BH Army and also within the VRS. What about this knowledge; was it an extended sort of knowledge or was it only sketchy or patchy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had the kind of information that we were able to obtain, we, or, rather, our people on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there's a whole series of documents, and had I known that it would raise problems, then I would have listed all the documents. But I think that there are documents signed by Mr. Petkovic talking about Serbs shooting. There are also documents stemming from the international community referring to what is done by the Serbs, and so on and so forth. So we have a series of documents showing that the conflict was not amongst two parties, but that all the parties were involved, and that's what I want to know. According to you, was it a conflict purely between Croats and Muslims or did it involve Croats and Muslims against the Serbs, or sometimes Muslims against the Serbs, Croats against the Serbs? So, you know, there are several possible cases.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That depends on the period of time we're talking about. There were clashes where the Muslims and the Croats fought the Serbs. That applied to most of the war. And there were certain clashes when the Serbs took steps against the Croats and the Muslims occasionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And possibly could you give us some dates, or don't you have specific dates that you can give us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I'll give it a try. Specifically in the Mostar area, speaking of an all-out war that broke out on the 30th of June, 1993, up until that point in time both Croats and Muslims, the HVO and the BH Army, had been fighting together against the Serbs. Afterward, Serbs fought the Croats and the Muslims, depending on the point in time, in the Konjic area specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a few minutes left. Ms. Alaburic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, I sincerely thank you for assuming the responsibility to ask these questions, saying that you were the one who initiated this exchange. It certainly wasn't my intention.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I believe we have sufficient time now for the next document on which I will be requiring your brief comments, P2019, 2019. These are minutes from a meeting held on the 21st of April, 1993, attended by representatives of the BH Army and the HVO alike. It was put together -- the document was put together by Tihomir Blaskic. What I want to know about is a particular sentence by Sefer Halilovic which was addressed to Petkovic, and Petkovic's reply. This is, roughly speaking, midway through the document. Sefer Halilovic says: "Your leading politicians advocate the creation of a Croat state in BH territory." Petkovic replies, I quote: "Well, you ought to be reasonable enough to know that Croatia cannot go for the annexation of BH territory, in which case it would lose some of its own territory. Nevertheless, you are simply looking for reasons to disagree." Mr. Jasak, given your familiarity with General Petkovic, and the fact that you were an intelligence officer with the Main Staff, can you please comment on General Petkovic's clarification?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Petkovic's explanation is perfectly understandable. Croatia was in no position to consider altering its borders in any way in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. It was the Badinter Commission that determined the borders, and the borders were not to be changed in any way. The borders as established under AVNOJ, A-V-N-O-J. Croatia was perfectly aware that with one-third of its own territory under someone else's control, any attempt it may have made at messing around with the borders would have threatened its very existence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, who was controlling this one-third of Croatia's territory that you have just referred to?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about these Serbs in Croatia; did they want to carve off this one-third of Croatia and see it annexed by Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the plan. It was the plan for a Greater Serbia. The Karlovac-Karlobag border was supposed to mark its western border, western-most border.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: By raising the issue of Bosnia-Herzegovina's borders, would that not also raise the issue of Croatia's borders, and would that not have, in a way, helped the Serbs to achieve their own goal in Croatia, in terms of taking away part of Croatia's territory?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that avenue would then have been open.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, it's 7.00. I think it's a good time for us to stop. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. So you'll come tomorrow morning at 9.00, Witness. You'll have a hearing from 9.00 until 1.45, and on Thursday we'll start at 4.15 [as interpreted] and we'll most likely end up at 6.00 p.m. I don't think that we will be done with the cross-examinations from the other accused. We'll continue on Monday, and the Prosecutor will get his six hours. Next week, we have four days, so we'll have enough time to conclude. So please do not forget tomorrow to be back here at 9.00. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of January, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
